prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No building has been grown and self-assembled from living materials, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000 such buildings is unmet. The largest mycelium structure found is the temporary 2014 Hy-Fi tower of 10,000 grown bricks, assembled by hand and composted after one summer (https://www.dezeen.com/2014/02/06/hy-fi-by-the-living-at-moma-ps1/). Self-growing fungal-bacterial bricks remain at lab scale (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9845837/); the EU Fungateria project aims next to grow buildings in a controlled way (https://projects.research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/en/print/pdf/node/13832); DARPA's Engineered Living Materials programme closed after laboratory research only (https://www.darpa.mil/research/programs/engineered-living-materials). The nearest commercial product, bacterial self-healing concrete from Basilisk, repairs cracks but does not grow structure (https://rics.org/news-insights/building-a-sustainable-future-the-incredible-potential-of-self-healing-concrete). Honest limit: biosafety of engineered strains is unresolved, and tasks reproducing mycelium bricks or self-healing concrete are known work needing their own basis.
